thread:
incident-bot: PAGER -> control-plane | elevated 5xx rate observed across auth & org-lookup routes. 5xx spike started ~2401234500. Paging oncall @maria :rotating_light:

maria: I'm awake, looking now. What metrics do we have?

sam: saw 502/504s hitting auth-proxy and org-lookup multiply. Grafana: auth-service 5xx rate up x6, p95 latency spiked to 1.2s.

joel: logs show a clear fanout to org-lookup, lots of upstream timeouts. Example: `auth->org-lookup` calls timing out at 1s then 504.

emma: Also seeing a surge of 429 from billing-service proxied through gateway around the same time. Could be cascade.

maria: running quick curl to health endpoints and auth token cache size
```
curl -sS -D- https://controlplane.internal/v1/health | head -n 20
# auth-proxy: 200
# org-lookup: 200
# but auth-proxy logs a lot of 502s when validating tokens
```

sam: tailing auth-proxy logs: `WARN auth-proxy: token-validate timeout, upstream org-lookup 504 for user lookup` repeating.

joel: hypothesis: org-lookup cache missed and we got a cache-stampede -> org-lookup pool exhausted -> timeouts -> auth fails -> gateway surfaces 5xx. Also billing rate limiting might amplify.

oncall-sre: @maria escalate to mitigation runbook 3 (control-plane dependency cascade). Start circuit breaker and route fallback for auth.

maria: applying quick mitigation: enabling auth-proxy local cache and rate-limiting org-lookup fanout (temporary)
```
# applying config via deploy bot
deploy-bot: deploying config auth-proxy:enable_local_cache=true,org-lookup:fanout_limit=8
# rolling update in progress
```

emma: pushed a temporary circuit breaker on org-lookup (opens at >50% errors) and increased retry backoff.

sam: after config push, 5xx rate dropped ~40% in last 30s but still above baseline. p95 latency improved to ~700ms.

joel: digging into Redis metrics for org-lookup cache — noticed large evictions around 2401234450 and sudden drops in hit-rate. Possible cache eviction storm after a spike.

maria: can we warm the cache with most frequent org ids? I can kick off a background warm job.

emma: starting a controlled cache-warm job - seeding top 1000 org ids to auth-proxy local cache (background task). Progress logs below:
```
[2401234590] cache-warm: seeded 200/1000
[2401234620] cache-warm: 600/1000
```

sam: adding temporary routing fallback: requests that fail org-lookup will use stale-cache TTL=5m before returning auth error (safer for UX). Config change pushed.

maria: customer impact assessment: internal metrics indicate 8% of API calls returned 5xx at peak; external error pages reported by 3 enterprise customers (sales ticket ids #4321, #4322). Some clients saw token validation failures causing UI errors. No data loss reported.

joel: mitigation checklist: 1) circuit-breaker on org-lookup (done) 2) local cache enable (done) 3) cache-warm job (in progress) 4) throttle upstream billing calls (partial) 5) monitor for recurrence (active)

oncall-sre: good. assign follow-ups: @joel investigate root cause of eviction (likely cache memory misconfig or workload change). @emma coordinate with infra to provision temporary scaled org-lookup replicas if needed. @maria own customer comms with support.

maria: drafting message for affected customers: short summary, mitigations, ETA for full resolution. Will post to support channel and update outstanding tickets.

sam: telemetry note: enable verbose sampling for failing requests for 10 minutes so we have traces for postmortem. Pushing rule now.
```
# telemetry:trace-sampling add service:auth-proxy filter:status>=500 duration=10m
```

emma: infra review - org-lookup DB showed increased query latency correlating with evictions; adding one read replica to reduce pressure. Initiating now.

joel: after warm and breaker, error rate down to 2% and trending down. p95 at ~350ms. Still monitoring for recurrence.

maria: handing off shift to @oncall-sre at 2401234700. Handoff notes:
- mitigations applied: local cache, breaker, fallback to stale-cache, cache-warm job kicked off, increased trace sampling
- customer impact: transient 5xx for ~8% of requests at peak; 3 enterprise customers reported issues; support notified
- next steps: investigate eviction root cause, consider permanent cache tuning or capacity, review billing throttles

oncall-sre: acknowledged, taking over. Will keep watch and escalate to platform pager if we see >3% sustained 5xx for 10m.

maria: thanks team :heart: please add any late notes here.

sam: note for postmortem - capture sequence: traffic surge -> cache evictions -> org-lookup pool exhaustion -> timeouts -> auth 5xx cascade -> billing rate-limit interactions -> amplified errors.

joel: uploading snapshots and logs to incident ticket INC-2401. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2401

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and set severity=P2. Auto-postmortem scheduled in 72h.

oncall-sre: closing active pager for now. Leaving monitoring alerts at elevated sensitivity for 2h.

maria: closing thread from my side, leave any follow-ups in INC-2401.
